extraction.summary: The authors propose a canonical scalar in flat FLRW Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, with V(phi)=V0 exp(-kappa lambda phi)+m_phi^2 phi^2/2 and a Gaussian f(phi) centered at the potential minimum. A transient nonminimal coupling is claimed to amplify late-time scalar oscillations so the effective equation of state crosses -1 before tending to a de Sitter-like future. The paper combines background autonomous-system numerics with linear scalar/tensor sound-speed expressions. Its displayed examples are initial-condition and parameter trajectories, not fits to DESI, supernova, CMB, or gravitational-wave data. The model's useful claim is conditional on a narrow stability domain and on resolving source-level equation inconsistencies recorded below.

ideas.title: A hybrid exponential-quadratic scalar potential produces a temporary oscillatory epoch
ideas.author_proposal: The potential V(phi)=V0 exp(-kappa lambda phi)+m_phi^2 phi^2/2 has a tunable minimum. A field initially Hubble-frozen can roll toward it and oscillate for a finite interval; the exponential term can later carry it toward a de Sitter-like branch.
ideas.reported_fit_or_measurement: None. Figure 1 uses illustrative parameter choices, including V0=10^-60 and kappa=1; these are not inferred values.

equations.expression: V(phi)=V0 exp(-kappa lambda phi)+(1/2)m_phi^2 phi^2; kappa lambda V0=m_phi^2 phi_c/exp(-kappa lambda phi_c); V_{,phi phi}(phi_c)=m_phi^2(1+lambda kappa phi_c)>0.
equations.definitions_and_domain: phi_c is a stationary point; the final inequality is the local-minimum condition. kappa is the inverse Planck mass in the action; lambda and m_phi are model parameters. No posterior or physical-unit calibration is supplied.

equations.expression: delta_phi proportional to exp(-3Ht/2) cos(omega_phi t+varphi), omega_phi=sqrt(m_eff^2-9H^2/4), m_eff^2=m_phi^2(1+lambda kappa phi_c).
equations.definitions_and_domain: Local homogeneous perturbation around phi_c; H and effective mass are treated as approximately constant for the damped-oscillator expression. Oscillations require m_eff>3H/2. The displayed solution fixes an unstated amplitude normalization.

ideas.reader_inference: The oscillation is a late-time transient mechanism rather than an early-dark-energy component or a unified early/late scalar history. Its existence alone does not determine a data-preferred trajectory.
ideas.description: The potential V(phi)=V0 exp(-kappa lambda phi)+m_phi^2 phi^2/2 has a tunable minimum. A field initially Hubble-frozen can roll toward it and oscillate for a finite interval; the exponential term can later carry it toward a de Sitter-like branch.

ideas.title: A localized Gauss-Bonnet coupling changes the effective pressure near the scalar minimum
ideas.author_proposal: A Gaussian coupling f(phi)=xi0 exp[-kappa^2(phi-phi_c)^2/(2 sigma^2)] is largest near the minimum and weakens as the field leaves it. Through the effective pressure term, the authors propose that it can amplify oscillations and produce repeated crossings of w_eff=-1 even though the canonical scalar's uncoupled w_phi stays at or above -1.
ideas.reported_fit_or_measurement: The paper reports numerical trajectories in selected parameter/initial-condition ranges; it reports no observational fit or measured phantom-crossing parameters.

equations.definitions_and_domain: sigma is the coupling width, xi0 its amplitude, and phi_c the potential minimum. The source does not provide a fitted value or uncertainty for either coupling parameter.

equations.expression: w_phi^eff=[(1/2)dot(phi)^2-V+8H f_{,phi} dot(phi)(dot(H)+H^2)]/[(1/2)dot(phi)^2+V]. Near the minimum the source writes w_phi^eff approximately -1+[8H/V](kappa^2 delta(phi)/sigma^2) f dot(delta(phi)) H^2 q.
equations.definitions_and_domain: The approximation assumes a transition epoch with potential energy dominating kinetic energy, homogeneous delta(phi), and the local Gaussian expansion. q=-1-dot(H)/H^2; the authors discuss q<0 near the acceleration transition. This does not establish a fitted history.
equations.confidence: high, subject to the separate Eq. (2.14) source inconsistency

ideas.reader_inference: The coupling can produce an effective phantom equation of state without a negative canonical kinetic term, but this is a modified-gravity background statement; it does not establish a healthy complete scalar perturbation sector or UV completion.

ideas.title: The autonomous background system has radiation/matter saddles and scalar-dominated equilibrium manifolds
ideas.author_proposal: The authors define a six-variable autonomous system and use its critical points plus numerical trajectories to describe a radiation-to-matter-to-scalar history.
ideas.reported_fit_or_measurement: P3 (radiation) and P4 (matter) are reported as saddles. P1 is scalar dominated with y_*+A_*=1 and free z,u; P2 has A_*=0 and a free z. The Appendix argues these are equilibrium manifolds with transverse attraction and neutral tangent directions where the nonzero eigenvalues are negative. Numerical trajectories approach de Sitter-like w_eff=-1 in selected domains. These are not a global proof or data fit.

equations.expression: x=kappa dot(phi)/(sqrt(6)H), y=kappa^2 V0 exp(-kappa lambda phi)/(3H^2), A=kappa^2 m_phi^2 phi^2/(6H^2), z=kappa phi, u=8kappa^2 H^2 f; Omega_r=kappa^2 rho_r/(3H^2), Omega_m=kappa^2 rho_m/(3H^2), z_c=kappa phi_c.
equations.definitions_and_domain: Prime is d/dN for N=ln(a). The paper also uses A for the lapse perturbation in Sec. V and explicitly warns these are different A variables in a footnote.
The Friedmann constraint eliminates Omega_r and requires 0<=Omega_r<=1 for the physical trajectories discussed.

equations.expression: The autonomous evolution equations are Eqs. (4.6)-(4.11), with z'=sqrt(6)x and Omega_m'=-2 Omega_m dot(H)/H^2-3Omega_m; dot(H)/H^2 is closed by Eqs. (4.3)-(4.4).
equations.definitions_and_domain: The vector field contains 1/z in x' and A', and the authors note apparent divergence as z->0 unless A->0; numerical solver stiffness is also reported for some initial conditions.
equations.confidence: medium; the long rational vector field was checked against HTML MathML/TeX and PDF layout but is not recopied here

ideas.reader_inference: Appendix A's equilibrium-manifold argument gives transverse attraction, not convergence to one fixed point along neutral directions. Fig. 3's gray algebraic curves are not integrated cosmological histories; the blue/red curves are the ODE trajectories.

ideas.title: Phantom-crossing trajectories occupy a parameter-dependent sound-speed and tensor-kinetic domain
ideas.author_proposal: The authors use linear scalar and tensor perturbations to identify trajectories they describe as free from ghosts and gradient instabilities.
ideas.reported_fit_or_measurement: For the Fig. 6(i) example lambda=0.31, the text reports -1.5<w_eff<-0.5 and c_s^2 roughly 0.5-1, while c_T^2 rapidly varies and crosses zero and values above 1; it cites this case as violating |c_T^2-1|<10^-16. For Fig. 6(ii), lambda=0.006 and the stated initial conditions give w_eff near -1.2, c_T^2 minimum about 0.5 and c_s^2 close to 1; the authors report Q_T>0 and no negative sound speeds for this trajectory. No observational data fit establishes preference for either branch.

equations.expression: The PDF/HTML prints c_T^2=[1-8 dot(H) f_{,phi} dot(phi)-8H^2 f_{,phiphi} dot(phi)^2]/[1-8 dot(H) f_{,phi} dot(phi)] in Eq. (5.2); Eq. (5.6) separately defines Q_T=1-8H dot(f)>0 and Eq. (5.3) uses factors of (1-8H dot(f)).
equations.definitions_and_domain: The source says these expressions assume kappa^2=1. The denominator discrepancy between Eq. (5.2) and Q_T/Eq. (5.3) is preserved as printed and blocks unqualified use.

equations.expression: The source's stated condition is 0<=c_s^2,c_T^2<=1 and Q_T=1-8H dot(f)>0; c_s^2 and c_T^2 are presented as ratios N/D in Eqs. (5.4)-(5.5).
equations.definitions_and_domain: Negative squared speed is identified with gradient instability. The upper bound of 1 is an additional subluminality requirement, not the nonnegative-speed condition itself. No current-data qualification is supplied.

ideas.reader_inference: The lambda=0.006 curve is the least problematic displayed example, but its acceptability still depends on the printed equations being correct and on an explicit scalar kinetic/ghost check. Eq. (5.6) does not name a separate scalar kinetic coefficient; Sol should determine whether the paper's QT-only ghost statement is sufficient. The lambda=0.31 plotted tensor speed is visibly outside the cited GW bound and exceeds unity for part of the plotted interval.

caveats.locator: PDF p.4 Eq. (2.14); compare Eqs. (2.13) and (2.15); HTML #S2.E13-#S2.E15
caveats.detail: Eq. (2.14) prints the energy-transfer factor (H^2+dot(H)^2), while Eq. (2.13) defines G=24H^2(H^2+dot(H)) and Eq. (2.15) uses (H^2+dot(H)). The PDF rendering and HTML TeX both show the squared dot(H) in Eq. (2.14). This is retained as a printed source inconsistency, not silently repaired.

caveats.locator: PDF pp.3-4 Eqs. (2.1), (2.4), (2.9), and p.10 note before Eq. (5.2)
caveats.detail: The action and metric equation state G_mu_nu=kappa^2 T_mu_nu, but Eq. (2.9) prints 3H^2=rho_phi+rho_m+rho_r+24H^3 dot(f) without an overall kappa^2. A later perturbation calculation explicitly assumes kappa^2=1, but the background section does not state that convention. The equation may use an unstated normalization; this needs source review.

Eq. (5.2) prints the tensor-speed denominator as 1-8 dot(H) f_{,phi} dot(phi), while Eq. (5.6) defines Q_T=1-8H dot(f) and Eq. (5.3) uses 1-8H dot(f). The paper's stability evaluation must be checked against the action before accepting the plotted stability window.

caveats.locator: PDF p.10 Eq. (5.6), p.12 Sec. V.1, and Fig. 6(i) on p.13
caveats.detail: Eq. (5.6) groups 0<=c_s^2,c_T^2<=1 under ghost/gradient avoidance, although the text and Fig. 6(i) discuss c_T^2 above 1 as superluminal. Negative squared speed is the gradient-instability condition; the upper bound is a separate subluminality criterion. The text also says the higher amplitude crosses the superluminal regime c_s^2>1 and then says c_s^2 stays in 0.5<=c_s^2<1; the plotted legend/curve identify the rapidly superluminal quantity as c_T^2, suggesting a source symbol typo.

caveats.locator: PDF p.10 Eq. (5.6), pp.12-14 Sec. V.1 and conclusion
caveats.detail: The explicit kinetic-sign quantity named in Eq. (5.6) is Q_T. The paper does not separately state a scalar kinetic coefficient/positivity condition there. The authors infer ghost absence for the displayed cases from small coupling and positive Q_T; Sol should check whether the scalar sector is fully covered by the equations used.

caveats.locator: PDF pp.7-13, Table I and Figs. 2-6
caveats.detail: Stability evidence is local to selected critical-point domains or numerical examples. Appendix A establishes transverse attraction to equilibrium manifolds with neutral tangent directions, not attraction to a unique point. Figure 3's gray curves are algebraic expressions, not integrated trajectories. None of the examples establishes observational preference, a CMB Hubble-tension solution, or a data-qualified history.
A is used both for the quadratic-potential dynamical variable and for the lapse perturbation; the authors flag this in a footnote. Preserve the distinction when transcribing equations.

usefulness.assessment: A useful, clearly scoped Einstein-scalar-GB mechanism and a strong source-review target. It overlaps the registered oscillating-scalar literature at the level of transient field oscillations, while adding a late-time localized curvature coupling and effective phantom crossing. It is not yet suitable for graph acceptance or candidate-design promotion because the displayed background/perturbation equations have source inconsistencies, scalar ghost coverage needs review, and the paper has no model-data fit.
usefulness.minimal_test: Before any numerical use, have Sol reconcile the printed Eq. (2.14), the Friedmann normalization, and the tensor-speed denominator in Eq. (5.2) against the action and original MathML/PDF; then check the scalar and tensor kinetic/sound-speed conditions along the explicitly shown lambda=0.006 trajectory. This reader performed no experiment or numerical reproduction.
usefulness.lost_scope: The paper gives no observational likelihood or fit, no uncertainty-qualified model parameters, no perturbation/data pipeline for CMB or structure constraints, and no demonstrated UV completion. The DESI/SN and GW statements are motivation or cited comparison only.

corrections.detail: With kappa inverse reduced Planck mass, [phi]=M, [V]=M^4, [f]=1. corrections.detail: Eq.(5.2) has dotH fphi phidot in the denominator, instead of H fdot, and its numerator is not the chain rule fddot=fphiphi phidot²+fphi phiddot. Its terms are dimensionally inconsistent before choosing units. The tensor kinetic/gradient action-consistency relation for the sign −fG is cT²=(1−8kappa² fddot)/(1−8kappa² H fdot). Substitution of the KG equation and Eq.(4.1) gives precisely the printed Eq.(5.5). Hence Eq.(5.2) is malformed, but this alone does not establish that plots computed from Eq.(5.5) are wrong. No author code or independent quadratic-action reconstruction was examined.

corrections.detail: At z0=zc, the source minimum relation requires A0/y0=lambda zc/2. Fig.6(i) has z0=zc=1.2, lambda=.31 and A0/y0=10^1.16≈14.45, whereas the required ratio is .186. Fig.6(ii) has ratio 10^1.15≈14.13, whereas lambda=.006 requires .0036. No normalization/H0 choice repairs these dimensionless ratios. Thus the examples do not simultaneously realize the displayed hybrid potential and a Gaussian centered on its potential minimum. A Gaussian with an independent center would be a changed branch, not a silent repair.

corrections.detail: Damped-cosine expressions require approximately constant/adiabatic H and effective mass and an unspecified amplitude; they are not exact for arbitrary time-varying H. Intrinsic canonical w_phi, the source exchange-reassigned w_phi^eff and total kinematic w_eff differ. Effective phantom crossing is not proof of a negative canonical kinetic term, healthy perturbations or a DESI/SN fit.
